section: Extending the OpenShift CLI with plugins
job_statement: When I need CLI functionality that the default oc commands do not provide, I want to extend the OpenShift CLI with custom plugins, so I can perform new and more complex tasks tailored to my workflow.
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
related_jobs: Manage applications using developer CLI commands
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to add custom CLI capabilities that address workflow-specific needs
Minimize the risk of conflicts with existing oc commands when writing plugins
Maximize the discoverability of installed plugins through oc plugin list
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 3931-4464 (Extending the OpenShift CLI with plugins assembly, including Writing CLI plugins and Installing and using CLI plugins modules)
notes: Small section with two procedures: writing a plugin (naming conventions, script structure) and installing/using a plugin (chmod, PATH placement, oc plugin list verification). Plugins cannot overwrite existing oc commands.

job_statement: When I want to add a custom command to the OpenShift CLI, I want to write a plugin script following the naming and structure conventions, so I can invoke my custom functionality through the oc command.
parent_job: Extend the OpenShift CLI with custom plugins
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to create a working plugin script that is recognized by the oc CLI
Minimize the likelihood of naming conflicts with built-in oc commands
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 4353-4401 (Writing CLI plugins procedure: naming conventions oc-/kubectl- prefix, file name to command mapping, sample Bash plugin)
notes: Covers naming conventions (oc- or kubectl- prefix, underscores for dashes), provides a sample Bash plugin. Links to Kubernetes sample-cli-plugin and cli-runtime repositories.

job_statement: When I have written a custom CLI plugin, I want to install it and verify it is recognized, so I can use it as part of my normal oc command workflow.
parent_job: Extend the OpenShift CLI with custom plugins
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
Write a custom CLI plugin
desired_outcomes: Minimize the number of steps to make a plugin available system-wide
Minimize the time to verify a plugin is correctly installed and invocable
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 4412-4464 (Installing and using CLI plugins procedure: chmod +x, place in PATH, oc plugin list verification, invoke the command)
notes: Prerequisites: oc installed, plugin file with oc- or kubectl- prefix. Steps: make executable, place in PATH, verify with oc plugin list, invoke.

job_statement: When I am developing and deploying applications on OpenShift, I want to use the oc developer CLI commands to create, build, deploy, debug, and manage my applications, so I can efficiently manage the full application lifecycle from the command line.
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
Log in to an OpenShift cluster
related_jobs: Extend the OpenShift CLI with custom plugins
Manage a cluster using administrator CLI commands
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to find the correct oc command and syntax for a given developer task
Maximize the percentage of application lifecycle tasks achievable from the CLI without switching to the web console
Minimize errors caused by incorrect command syntax or missing options
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 4467-8017 (OpenShift CLI developer command reference assembly, auto-generated reference of ~100 oc developer commands with descriptions and examples)
notes: This is a large auto-generated reference section. Commands are listed alphabetically, each with a description and example usage. Covers the full developer command surface area. The user_stories below group these commands by functional purpose.

job_statement: When I need to create and deploy a new application on OpenShift, I want to use CLI commands for application creation, build configuration, and deployment management, so I can go from source code to a running application.
parent_job: Manage applications using developer CLI commands
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
Log in to an OpenShift cluster
Have access to a project
related_jobs: Debug and troubleshoot running applications via CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time from source code to a running, accessible application
Minimize the number of manual steps required to create application resources
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 6817-6912 (oc new-app), 6872-6912 (oc new-build), 7879-7904 (oc start-build), 6927-6932 (oc new-project), 5408-5440 (oc expose), 5585-5607 (oc create)
notes: Groups commands: oc new-app (create application from source/image/template), oc new-build (create build config), oc start-build (trigger builds), oc new-project (create project), oc expose (expose services as routes). These are the primary commands for getting a new application running.

job_statement: When I need to manage deployment rollouts and scaling of my applications, I want to use CLI commands for rollout management, scaling, and rollback, so I can control how and when application updates are delivered.
parent_job: Manage applications using developer CLI commands
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
Have a deployed application
related_jobs: Create and deploy a new application via CLI
Configure application resource settings via CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to roll out, pause, resume, or undo a deployment change
Minimize downtime during application updates
Maximize confidence that a rollback can restore the previous working state
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 7235-7322 (oc rollout and subcommands: cancel, history, latest, pause, restart, resume, retry, status, undo), 7225-7235 (oc rollback), 7464-7492 (oc scale), 7813-7843 (oc set triggers)
notes: Groups commands: oc rollout (manage rollouts with cancel/history/latest/pause/restart/resume/retry/status/undo subcommands), oc rollback (revert to previous deployment), oc scale (adjust replica count), oc set triggers (configure deployment triggers), oc autoscale (create autoscaler).

job_statement: When I need to inspect, create, modify, or delete Kubernetes resources, I want to use CLI commands for resource CRUD operations, so I can manage the desired state of my cluster resources efficiently.
parent_job: Manage applications using developer CLI commands
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
Log in to an OpenShift cluster
related_jobs: Create and deploy a new application via CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to query, create, update, or remove any resource type
Minimize errors when applying resource changes by previewing diffs before applying
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 4900-4930 (oc annotate), 4968-4996 (oc apply and subcommands), 5585-5607 (oc create and subcommands), 6192-6230 (oc delete), 6231-6262 (oc describe), 6259-6278 (oc diff), 6274-6302 (oc edit), 5427-5482 (oc get), 6724-6756 (oc label), 6945-6975 (oc patch), 7190-7215 (oc replace), 7259-7274 (oc diff)
notes: Groups the resource management commands: oc get/describe/create/delete/edit/apply/patch/replace/annotate/label/diff/explain. These are the foundational CRUD operations used across all developer and admin workflows.

job_statement: When my application is not behaving as expected, I want to use CLI commands for debugging, log inspection, remote execution, and status checking, so I can diagnose and resolve issues in running workloads.
parent_job: Manage applications using developer CLI commands
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
Have a running application or pod
related_jobs: Configure application resource settings via CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to identify the root cause of an application failure
Minimize the need to recreate issues locally by enabling remote debugging
Maximize the ability to inspect logs and events for any container in a pod
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 6152-6192 (oc debug), 6791-6817 (oc logs), 6322-6362 (oc exec), 7388-7418 (oc rsh), 7413-7432 (oc rsync), 7057-7092 (oc port-forward), 5064-5070 (oc attach), 6298-6326 (oc events), 7908-7926 (oc status), 5551-5585 (oc cp)
notes: Groups debugging/troubleshooting commands: oc debug (launch debug pod), oc logs (view container logs), oc exec (run commands in containers), oc rsh (remote shell), oc rsync (file sync), oc port-forward (port forwarding), oc attach (attach to running process), oc events (view events), oc status (project overview), oc cp (copy files).

job_statement: When I need to adjust environment variables, resource limits, probes, volumes, or other configuration on my deployed applications, I want to use the oc set commands, so I can update application configuration without manually editing YAML.
parent_job: Manage applications using developer CLI commands
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
Have deployed application resources
related_jobs: Debug and troubleshoot running applications via CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to update application configuration properties
Minimize the risk of YAML syntax errors by using targeted set commands
Maximize consistency of configuration changes across multiple resources
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 6594-6638 (oc set env), 6658-6686 (oc set image), 6685-6718 (oc set image-lookup), 6715-6750 (oc set probe), 6736-6770 (oc set resources), 6766-6800 (oc set route-backends), 7843-7883 (oc set volumes), 6555-6578 (oc set data), 6575-6598 (oc set deployment-hook), 7776-7800 (oc set serviceaccount), 7791-7813 (oc set subject), 7763-7780 (oc set selector)
notes: Groups the oc set subcommands: set env, set image, set image-lookup, set probe, set resources, set route-backends, set volumes, set data, set deployment-hook, set build-hook, set build-secret, set triggers, set selector, set serviceaccount, set subject. These provide targeted modifications without full YAML editing.

job_statement: When I need to manage container images for my applications, I want to use CLI commands for image importing, tagging, mirroring, and inspection, so I can control which images are available and used in my deployments.
parent_job: Manage applications using developer CLI commands
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
Have access to image registries
related_jobs: Create and deploy a new application via CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to import external images into OpenShift image streams
Minimize the complexity of mirroring images between registries
Maximize visibility into image metadata and layers
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 6706-6710 (oc import-image), 7926-7960 (oc tag), 6505-6548 (oc image append), 6544-6597 (oc image extract), 6593-6618 (oc image info), 6614-6680 (oc image mirror), 7190-7198 (oc registry login)
notes: Groups image management commands: oc import-image (import from registry to image stream), oc tag (tag images into image streams), oc image append/extract/info/mirror (image manipulation and inspection), oc registry login (authenticate to registry).

job_statement: When I need to authenticate to an OpenShift cluster or verify my permissions, I want to use CLI commands for login, session management, and authorization checking, so I can securely access the cluster and confirm I have the required permissions for my tasks.
parent_job: Manage applications using developer CLI commands
prerequisites: Install and configure the OpenShift CLI
Have cluster credentials
related_jobs: Manage and inspect cluster resources via CLI
desired_outcomes: Minimize the time to authenticate and start working with a cluster
Minimize permission-related errors by checking authorization before attempting operations
Maximize security by properly managing login sessions
evidence: cli_reference-combined.adoc, combined lines 6752-6784 (oc login), 6791-6795 (oc logout), 8003-8012 (oc whoami), 7067-7108 (oc auth can-i), 7108-7120 (oc auth reconcile), 7131-7140 (oc auth whoami), 6493-6498 (oc get-token), 7002-7020 (oc policy add-role-to-user), 7017-7044 (oc policy scc-review), 7039-7062 (oc policy scc-subject-review)
notes: Groups authentication/authorization commands: oc login, oc logout, oc whoami, oc auth can-i, oc auth reconcile, oc auth whoami, oc get-token, oc policy add-role-to-user, oc policy scc-review, oc policy scc-subject-review. Also includes oc create token for service account tokens.
